$comment: Every hook is registered in EXEC form (command + args), never shell form. Claude Code
expands ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} itself, into both fields, before any shell sees it — so
there is no shell and no quoting, and one entry is correct on Gentoo, Debian and
Windows alike. Shell form would need $VAR on bash and $env:/%VAR% on Windows, where
Claude Code falls back to PowerShell if Git Bash is absent. scripts/check-hooks.mjs
fails the build on a shell-form entry, on a registration pointing at a file that does
not exist, and on a hook file that no event registers.
The codegraph `UserPromptSubmit` hook is deliberately NOT declared here: it already
lives in ~/.claude/settings.json, and project settings merge with user settings, so a
second declaration would inject the same context twice.
guard-symbol-search.mjs, by contrast, belongs HERE and not in user settings. It is a
statement about THIS tree — that .codegraph/ indexes it, and that a search for a symbol
in it is answered better by the index than by grep — so it has to travel with the repo
and apply to whoever is working in the checkout, not to one machine's user. It carries
the only timeout above 10 s among the PreToolUse guards, because on a candidate it
spawns one `codegraph query` (~190 ms warm); a non-candidate search never gets that far.
The 15 s is a real bound the hook is written against, not a round number — but it took two
fixes to actually BE one, and both are load-bearing. resolveLauncher() memoises its result
INCLUDING a null, and decide() stops consulting the index once GATE3_BUDGET_MS is spent.
Without those, probing and querying both ran once per identifier on the line: measured at
32 s for eight identifiers with every launcher candidate hanging, against this very 15 s.
The arithmetic that holds now: one probe round (4 x 2 s) plus one 5 s query = 13 s, and the
10 s budget means no second query is ever started after it. Re-measured at 4 s.
Raising any of those constants without raising this one buys back the stall — and it fails
OPEN, so the search runs and nothing says why the guard went quiet.
Machine-specific overrides belong in .claude/settings.local.json, which .gitignore
already excludes.
